method: int8 ONNX query embeddings vs fp32 PyTorch query embeddings, both searched against index-v3's fp32-built whitened gallery
note_int8_rejected: Dynamic int8 quantisation was measured and REJECTED. Control on the same 40 queries: ONNX fp32 = 0.7500/0.8500 (delta +0.00p vs PyTorch), ONNX int8 = 0.0500/0.1250 (delta -70.00p). The fp32 control matching PyTorch exactly proves the measurement pipeline is correct, so the collapse is a genuine quantisation effect, not a harness bug. Dynamic int8 weight quantisation is known to be destructive for ViTs because attention needs more dynamic range than int8 weights provide. The app therefore ships fp32 (346.5 MB).
